acceptance: Measurement table in the ADR: per sampled page, docstring-derived vs signature-derived content
Public-surface list derived from code, not from docstrings
Decision A/B/C recorded with owner approval
Every current reference URL mapped to a target (kept path or redirect page)
api-docs lane impact stated (what publication/site-deploy copies after the change)
description:
Today docs/api.rst and docs/reference/python-api/** (27 .rst pages) use automodule, autoclass and autosummary with napoleon and viewcode. publication-deploy.yml also copies api.html, _modules and reference/python-api into an api-docs lane. Docstrings are being removed from the project (COMMENT-POLICY-001), so docstring-driven generation (griffe, autodoc) has a shrinking and eventually empty source.

Measure, then decide:
(1) How much rendered API content comes from docstrings today versus signatures and type hints alone. Sample at least the benchmarks/* and platforms/* pages.
(2) Which symbols are actually the supported public surface: benchbox.__all__ and what the docs and examples import.
Options:
A. Retire the generated reference. Replace it with hand-written "Python API" guide pages for the supported surface, backed by examples that example-validation already checks.
B. A signatures-only reference generated by static analysis (names, signatures, type hints, module layout, no prose), plus option A's guides.
C. Keep a reduced Sphinx autodoc lane just for the API. Rejected unless A and B both fail; it keeps Python doc tooling alive.
Record the choice in the ADR (D7), with the URL plan for every existing reference URL (keep the path with new content, or add a redirect page).
